bug_semantics: CIPster's generic attribute encode/decode treats a kCipByteArray and a companion kCipByteArrayLength as views over the same ByteBuf, which stores only start/limit and derives size() as limit-start with no immutable backing-store capacity. A remote SetAttributeSingle on a writable kCipByteArrayLength reaches CipAttribute::SetAttrData -> DecodeData(kCipByteArrayLength), which rebuilds the shared ByteBuf as ByteBuf(bb->data(), aBuf.get16()) from an attacker-supplied uint16 and thereby poisons limit. A subsequent GetAttributeSingle on the aliased kCipByteArray (GetAttrData -> EncodeData) over-reads the real allocation, and a subsequent SetAttributeSingle (SetAttrData -> DecodeData(kCipByteArray)) constructs a BufWriter from the inflated end() and memcpy-writes past the backing buffer. Stock Assembly instance attr 4 registers kCipByteArrayLength as gettable-only (isSetableSingle default false), so the default sample is not the demonstrated path; the public AttributeInsert API can register both types writable against one ByteBuf, which is the confirmed API-enabled attack.
flaw_origin: 90721b00e44e461d14501bb20714a4d71d9e18e4 (2018-07-24, Dick Hollenbeck) first added non-standard enum kCipByteArrayLength=0xA5, replaced the old CipByteArray {length,data} struct with a new ByteBuf {start,limit} view, and wrote DecodeData(kCipByteArrayLength) as *bb = ByteBuf(bb->data(), aBuf.get16()) plus EncodeData/DecodeData(kCipByteArray) that copy according to that ByteBuf size. Immediate parent d06f16ea2ef9a10b894324a80ec686443708ed59 has no kCipByteArrayLength, no ByteBuf class, and no wire-driven length rewrite; its kCipByteArray path memcpy'd a caller-pre-set length. Those 2018 lines survived, modulo typedefs, through advisory commit 1802525 until the 2026 CipByteArray capacity split.
